Yes, Boss — you **should** learn trees before going into graphs.  

Here’s why (straightforward reasoning):  

- **Tree is a special type of graph.**  
  A tree is basically a graph with no cycles and exactly one path between any two nodes. So if you already know trees, a big part of graph theory becomes easier.  

- **Concept overlap.**  
  Things like nodes, edges, traversal (DFS, BFS), parent-child relations — all of these show up in graphs too, but in a more general form.  

- **Stepping stone.**  
  Trees are simpler → no cycles, one root, clear hierarchy.  
  Graphs are more complex → cycles, multiple paths, directed/undirected edges, weighted edges, etc.  
  If you skip trees and jump into graphs, you’ll get lost in complexity.  

👉 My advice:  
1. Learn **trees first** (binary tree, BST, tree traversals).  
2. Then move to **graphs** (adjacency list, adjacency matrix, DFS/BFS on graphs, shortest path, etc.).  

This way, you build intuition gradually instead of hitting the graph wall head-on.
